It names one premises, an establishment or a site, by its name and at its locality: `place.name` is that name and `place.locality` the town. Or it says plainly, in its title or its summary, that it is a kind of place and names no premises: then `place.name` holds the kind, for example `motel`, and `place.locality` the town. Where you are given places to stay from map data for a town, a premises you name there is one of those, under the name it is given, if any of them fits the party. A kind of place is the fallback, for a town whose list is empty or where nothing in it fits.

      "location": { "kind": "at", "place": { "name": "...", "locality": "... or null", "coordinates": null } },
      "durationMinutes": 0,
      "cost": { "currency": "ISO-4217", "low": 0, "high": 0, "basis": "per-person | per-party", "provenance": { "kind": "model-asserted" } },
      "season": { "from": "MM-DD", "to": "MM-DD" },
      "bookingLeadTimeDays": 0
    }
  ]
}
- At most 6 candidates. Fewer is a fine answer; an empty list is a fine answer.
- Anything you do not know is null. A duration nobody measured is null, not a plausible ninety minutes. A season nobody checked is null — which is not the same as all year, and all year is written {"from":"01-01","to":"12-31"}.
- Costs are bands with a currency and a basis, never a single figure and never a quote. Do not total anything.
- A slot that says "not answered" is unknown to you. Say in the summary what you could not account for, and propose anyway. Never invent the answer and never refuse to propose.
- Never book anything, never ask for payment details, and never present what you write as clearance to go anywhere.
- Every candidate is a movement, so its location is {"kind":"between","from":{...},"to":{...}} with **both** ends as places. Endpoints in the title are not endpoints, and a candidate that puts them there is discarded.
- This trip has 4 days.
- **Nothing you propose may be longer than 480 minutes.** That is the party's own answer about how much a day holds, translated into minutes. Something longer has to be split into parts that each fit, or not proposed — a candidate over that ceiling is discarded and the plan comes back missing this part of itself.

messages.content:
Here is the trip. It is everything you get.

Shape: backcountry
Leaving from: Québec City
Going to: Parc national de la Gaspésie
Dates: 3 nights somewhere between 2027-08-15 and 2027-09-15
Travellers: 2
Ages that change the plan: 34, 36
Access needs: not answered
Budget: shoestring, as a feeling rather than a figure
Appetite for effort: demanding
Roughest night they will accept: rustic
Would rule the trip out: Nothing that requires a river ford above the knee

About this backcountry:
Nights away from a road: 3
Shelter: hut
Most they will walk in a day: 16 km
Experience: some
In their words: We have done hut-to-hut in the Chic-Chocs once before, in fair weather. Neither of us has navigated in cloud and we would rather not learn on this trip.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hut-to-hut in the Chic-Chocs on marked trail, sheltered by Sépaq huts
candidatesAccepted.summary: Rustic refuge nights in huts keep gear light and match the experience they have already had. Hut spots are limited and late-summer weekends fill, so ask Sépaq about availability. Cloud-navigation is the real gap: stick to well-marked sections and have a turn-back rule. Stream levels after rain could matter given the knee-deep ford limit, so ask the park about crossings before committing. Cost is a rough band and not a quote. Kit: stove, sleeping bag, rain gear, water treatment, paper map and compass.
